CVE-2026-107494.title: Unbounded QUIC RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID Frame Sending Queue
CVE-2026-107494.description:
Issue summary: The QUIC stack queues a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame also for
retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames. This allows a remote malicious
QUIC stack to queue an unlimited number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.

Impact summary: A malicious remote QUIC peer can trigger an out-of-memory
condition causing a Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: The earlier fix for CVE-2026-84784 was not complete. It
failed to ignore retransmissions of the NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame. The QUIC
implementation created and inserted a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame for every
retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame it received and there was no limit
on how many RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames were queued.
This allows a malicious remote QUIC stack to trigger an out-of-memory (OOM)
condition.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation is outside the
OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

In all prior released versions of FRRouting, the OSPFv3 (for IPv6) implementation does not check that OSPFv3 packets have a link-local source address and either a link-local destination or one of the protocol multicast destination groups. CVE-2026-126576.title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unchecked exponent length in binary REAL decoding
CVE-2026-126576.description:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unchecked exponent length in binary REAL decoding.

Binary REAL decoding never bounds-checks the exponent length against the available content. For a minimal one-byte binary REAL, the exponent byte is read from outside the element, making the mantissa length -1. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the mantissa is nearly all of the input that follows the element. The long-form exponent path also omits the extra length octet when sizing the mantissa.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a list of such values, as each mantissa loop iterates over the remaining input. The decoded values are also computed from bytes outside each element.

CVE-2026-99449.title: usb: gadget: fix refcount underflow in gadgetfs_bind() error path
CVE-2026-99449.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

usb: gadget: fix refcount underflow in gadgetfs_bind() error path

gadgetfs_bind() calls get_dev() only on the success path, but
gadgetfs_unbind() called from the enomem error label unconditionally
calls put_dev(). When bind fails (e.g. ENOMEM), put_dev() fires
without a matching get_dev(), leaving the refcount unbalanced.

A subsequent close of the ep0 file descriptor calls dev_release() ->
put_dev() which hits zero and frees the object; then gadgetfs_kill_sb()
calls put_dev(the_device) again on the already-freed pointer, triggering
a refcount underflow and use-after-free.

Fix by calling get_dev() at the start of gadgetfs_bind(), before any
error path that invokes gadgetfs_unbind(), so the reference is always
balanced regardless of whether bind succeeds or fails.

CVE-2026-99535.title: ksmbd: prevent share root removal through empty paths
CVE-2026-99535.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: prevent share root removal through empty paths

A FileLinkInformation request can supply "/" as the new link name.
smb2_get_name() strips the trailing slash and passes an empty string to
ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_start_removing().

ksmbd_vfs_path_lookup() resolves an empty pathname as the configured share
path, without LOOKUP_BENEATH. With ReplaceIfExists set, smb2_create_link()
can therefore remove the share root from its parent before link creation
fails. An authenticated client with a writable share and DELETE access to
a file can trigger this if the share root is empty and the mapped user
has write and search permission on its parent directory.

Return -EINVAL for empty pathnames when for_remove is set, before
resolving the share path or acquiring removal resources. Ordinary lookups
continue to accept empty pathnames for opening the share root.

CVE-2026-99658.title: mm/mmu_notifier: finish non-blocking interval invalidation on error
CVE-2026-99658.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mmu_notifier: finish non-blocking interval invalidation on error

When an ordinary MMU notifier rejects a non-blocking invalidation, the
interval invalidation started beforehand is left unfinished: the caller
skips mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_end(). Subsequent interval notifier
operations can then wait forever.

The only in-tree trigger is nouveau SVM, which uses both notifier types
and rejects non-blocking invalidations. Reaping via the OOM reaper or
process_mrelease() can therefore leave the GPU fault worker stuck,
holding a reference that prevents the dying process's address space
and memory from being freed.

non-blocking invalidation, like mn_itree_invalidate() already does when
an interval notifier fails. Make that handling clearer in the
documentation of mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_start_nonblock().
